name: ScreenBar Halo 2
pros: Aluminum housing and puck give a substantial, premium feel
Puck rotates smoothly for intuitive, tactile brightness control
Front beam lights the desktop with minimal screen glare
cons: Power cord is fixed at roughly five feet, not removable
Wireless controller battery is non-replaceable, limiting long-term repair
Counterweight clip can loosen on thick or slick monitor bezels
desc: Traditional desk lamps consume workspace and cast glare across monitor displays. The Halo 2 mounts above the screen instead, pairing an aluminum housing with dual-zone LEDs—an asymmetric front beam and a diffused ambient backlight—to separate desktop illumination from screen reflection. Wireless dial control and a CRI above 95 support accurate color work without adding desk clutter.

name: Felt Desk Mat
pros: Rubber backing holds the mat and keyboard in one place
Felt top wipes clean and shakes off loose dust
Full-size mat fits a laptop, keyboard, and mouse together
cons: Felt can feel rough on bare skin during heavy use
Mat ships rolled and takes time to lie flat
Felt soaks up liquid, so spills need quick attention
desc: Hard desks make noise, scratch easily, and let keyboards slide out of place. This mat uses a dense felt top over a rubber base to hold gear still, covering 39.4 by 19.69 inches for a laptop, keyboard, and mouse. The felt also softens typing sound and gives the wrist a comfortable rest.

name: Under-Desk Cable Trays
pros: Steel build holds up to 11 lbs without bending or sagging
Open-frame design keeps power adapters ventilated and cool
Clears cords and power bricks off the floor for easy cleaning
cons: Mounts with screws, leaving holes if moved or removed later
Each 17-inch tray fits one power strip, tight for more
Overhead screw installation takes a drill and some effort
desc: Loose cords and power bricks pile up on the floor, catching feet and collecting dust. These steel trays mount under the desk in a pair, each rated to hold 11 pounds, with an open front for routing cables and adapters. The low profile keeps the setup out of sight and clear of the knees, while the wire-frame body lets power blocks stay cool.

name: MagGo 2-in-1 Wireless Charging Stand
pros: 15W Qi2 charging matches official MagSafe speeds for compatible phones
Charges a phone and earbuds together on one stand
Tilts 45° and rotates 360° for a custom viewing angle
cons: No wall adapter included, only the USB-C cable
Skips Apple Watch, charging only phones and earbuds
Earbud pad has no magnet, so buds can slide off
desc: A phone left flat on a nightstand blocks the screen and misses a charge. This stand holds the phone upright with 15W Qi2 charging, adds a second pad for earbuds, and tilts or rotates to any angle for StandBy mode. A weighted base with a non-slip grip keeps it steady when the phone is lifted off.

name: F75 75% Wireless Mechanical Keyboard
pros: Gasket mount and foam layers give a soft, quiet typing feel
Switches to 2.4GHz, Bluetooth, or wired USB-C on demand
Hot-swap sockets allow switch changes without soldering
4000mAh battery holds a long charge on wireless use
cons: ABS plastic case feels light and can flex under pressure
Companion software is basic and limited to Windows
Keycap legends block RGB light, hard to read in the dark
Some users report input lag during fast, competitive play
desc: Full-size keyboards take up desk space many setups can't spare. This 75% board keeps the arrow keys while trimming the rest, built on a gasket-mounted plate with layered foam for a soft, quiet keystroke. Hot-swap sockets accept 3-pin or 5-pin switches without soldering, and tri-mode wireless links up to five devices.
